overview: ResMed is a global leader in digital health and cloud-connected medical devices for sleep apnea, COPD and other chronic respiratory conditions, best known as the pioneer and market leader in CPAP therapy. The company designs, manufactures and sells flow generators (devices), masks/accessories and diagnostic products through its Sleep and Breathing Health segment, complemented by a Residential Care Software segment (Brightree, MEDIFOX DAN, and until a pending divestiture, MatrixCare) that provides cloud-based practice management software to home medical equipment, home health, hospice and senior living providers. ResMed is dual-listed (NYSE primary listing under RMD; ASX CDI listing, 10 CDIs = 1 NYSE share), reports in USD on a June fiscal year end, and sells in more than 140 countries from manufacturing hubs in Singapore, Australia, the US, Malaysia, China and France.

business_model.summary: ResMed generates a razor/razor-blade style annuity stream: an initial device sale is followed by recurring, high-margin replacement sales of masks, cushions, tubing and other consumables (patients typically replace masks every 3-12 months), supplemented by growing cloud-software subscription/SaaS revenue from its Residential Care Software segment. Device sales are quasi-recurring too, since CPAP machines are typically replaced every ~5 years and insurance/Medicare often mandates periodic resupply.

revenue_streams.name: Residential Care Software (Brightree, MEDIFOX DAN, MatrixCare)

business_model.customer_type: B2B2C: sells primarily to home medical equipment (HME) providers, durable medical equipment (DME) suppliers, hospitals and sleep clinics who then supply/bill the end patient; direct-to-patient home healthcare operations in Germany, Australia, New Zealand and South Korea; software segment sells B2B/enterprise SaaS to HME, home health, hospice and senior-living operators
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas (largest, majority of revenue) and Combined Europe, Asia & Other ('Rest of World'); FY2026 revenue $5.65B, up from $5.15B in FY2025 (~9-10% growth)

competitive_position.market_position: Global #1 in CPAP/sleep apnea devices and masks, with an estimated ~55-65% share of the global flow-generator/mask market following Philips Respironics' 2021 recall; also the #1 cloud-connected installed base in sleep therapy (35M+ patients on AirView, 12M+ on myAir) and a leading position in home medical equipment/residential care practice-management software via Brightree.

moat_factors.description: 35M+ cloud-connected devices and 12M+ myAir users generate proprietary real-world adherence data used for R&D, payor negotiations and AI-driven personalization (e.g., Smart Comfort), reinforcing product superiority and stickiness

moat_factors.factor: Switching costs / prescriber and HME relationships
moat_factors.description: Deep, decades-long relationships with sleep labs, HME providers and payors; Brightree/MatrixCare software embeds ResMed further into provider workflows (though MatrixCare is being divested)

First mover since 1989 CPAP commercialization; funds and publishes some of the largest real-world sleep apnea outcome studies (e.g., Lancet Respiratory Medicine 2025 mortality-reduction meta-analysis), reinforcing physician trust
Globally distributed, ISO 13485/MDSAP-certified manufacturing network (Singapore, Australia, US, Malaysia, China, France) supports cost leadership and supply resilience versus smaller rivals
FDA/MDR clearance requirements, quality system regulation (QMSR) and reimbursement coding create barriers for new entrants, though barriers are lower in software

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on US reimbursement policy (Medicare/Medicaid, DMEPOS competitive bidding) for a large share of revenue
Philips Respironics' eventual full return to the US market (post consent-decree/recall) could reintroduce meaningful price and share competition
GLP-1/anti-obesity drugs represent a structural, still-uncertain long-term demand risk given ~77% of OSA patients have comorbid obesity
Residential Care Software segment faces low barriers to entry, intense competition, and is being partially unwound (MatrixCare sale) after underperforming expectations as a synergy platform
Product recalls/field safety issues (Astral ventilator correction in 2026) create litigation, reputational and execution risk

growth_drivers: Large underdiagnosed/undertreated OSA population: an estimated 936M+ people globally have OSA (424M+ moderate-to-severe) with under 20% diagnosed in the US and under 10% in other markets
New diagnostic pathways to expand the funnel: NightOwl home sleep test and 2025 VirtuOx acquisition (independent diagnostic testing facility) streamline diagnosis-to-therapy conversion

GLP-1 drugs acting as a near-term tailwind rather than headwind so far: ResMed's own real-world data on 2.5M+ patients shows GLP-1 users are >10% more likely to initiate CPAP and have higher resupply rates, as physician visits for weight loss increase OSA screening
AI-enabled personalization: myAir Smart Comfort (first FDA-cleared AI-enabled OSA comfort-setting feature) and other AI/ML algorithms to improve adherence and differentiate product experience
Adjacent expansion beyond core sleep apnea: June 2026 acquisition of Noctrix (FDA De Novo-cleared restless legs syndrome neurostimulation device) extends the clinical sleep-health portfolio

Portfolio optimization/capital discipline: pending $490M sale of MatrixCare (announced June 2026, expected to close Q1 FY2027) sharpens focus on core sleep, breathing and connected home healthcare and funds continued buybacks/dividends

Structural payor tailwind from clinical evidence: 2025 Lancet meta-analysis showing PAP therapy cuts all-cause mortality 37% and cardiovascular mortality 54% supports reimbursement and physician referral patterns
Continued gross margin expansion (61.1% in FY2026, up from 59.4% in FY2025) from manufacturing efficiency, mix shift to higher-margin masks/accessories, and cost discipline
Strong capital returns: $1.0B returned to shareholders in FY2026 (buybacks + dividends), up more than 70% year-over-year, alongside $1.6B of free cash flow

business.description: Injectable (and prospectively oral) GLP-1 drugs are approved for OSA treatment in obese patients with moderate-to-severe OSA and are being marketed directly to consumers; sustained, significant weight loss could reduce OSA severity/incidence over time, denting long-term device and consumables demand even though near-term data shows a net positive (higher CPAP initiation/resupply among GLP-1 users)

Philips remains under a US consent decree following its 2021 CPAP recall; ResMed cannot predict the timing or scale of Philips' full market re-entry, which took significant share from Philips during the recall period and could reverse

2026 voluntary global correction on Astral 100/150 ventilators (supercapacitor leak risk causing fail-safe shutdown) triggered an FDA early alert; management guided to a ~130bps FY2027 revenue drag and ~$0.15 EPS hit from the corrective action
Simultaneous integration of VirtuOx (2025) and Noctrix (2026) acquisitions plus the pending $490M MatrixCare divestiture (expected close Q1 FY2027) increases operational complexity and execution risk
Consolidation among HME providers, DME suppliers and payors increases buyer negotiating power and pricing pressure
Low barriers to entry in Residential Care Software; multiple device competitors (Philips, F&P, Chinese manufacturers Yuyue/BMC/Apex) compete on price and features

financial.description: Company carries debt used partly to fund acquisitions/buybacks; rising rates could increase financing costs, though balance sheet remains solid (total debt ~$0.66B vs equity ~$6.6B at FY2026)
Meaningful international (non-US) revenue exposes results to USD strength/weakness; management explicitly flags reported vs constant-currency growth each quarter

financial.risk: Tax audits and evolving international tax law
financial.description: Ongoing tax audits in various jurisdictions, including on transferred/discontinued local operations, and aggressive pursuit by tax authorities globally

regulatory.description: Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement changes (DMEPOS Competitive Bidding Program Round 2028, Physician Fee Schedule conversion factor cuts, One Big Beautiful Bill Act's ~$930B Medicaid funding cut over 10 years) could reduce payments to providers and pricing for ResMed's products
Extensive FDA QMSR, EU MDR and other global regulatory regimes govern product clearance and manufacturing quality; the 2026 Astral correction illustrates the tangible cost of field safety actions

regulatory.risk: Fraud, abuse, anti-kickback, Stark Law exposure
regulatory.description: VirtuOx and Noctrix acquisitions newly subject ResMed to direct Medicare beneficiary-inducement rules and, for Noctrix, the Stark Law as a DME/DHS supplier

regulatory.risk: Data privacy, AI and cybersecurity regulation
regulatory.description: HIPAA, GDPR/UK GDPR (fines up to 4% of global turnover), state privacy laws, EU AI Act (fines up to 7% of turnover) and a growing patchwork of state AI laws increase compliance cost and liability as ResMed embeds more AI/cloud health data features
Proposed VA rule changes to sleep apnea disability ratings could reduce veteran incentive to pursue/maintain CPAP treatment

macro.description: Products manufactured across Singapore, Malaysia, China, Australia, US and France are exposed to new or increased US tariffs and broader global trade disruption, though current tariff relief for ResMed's product categories was reaffirmed in April 2025
Reliance on single-source suppliers for certain components (including semiconductor chips and magnets) creates vulnerability to shortages

macro.risk: Healthcare consumer spending / insurance coverage cycles
macro.description: Device is largely insurance-reimbursed rather than pure discretionary spend, giving relative macro resilience, but coverage criteria and patient cost-sharing can still affect adoption in downturns

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Large, structurally underpenetrated global sleep apnea and COPD markets (est. 936M+ people with some OSA, 480M+ with COPD) with low diagnosis rates support multi-year volume growth; GLP-1 drugs are reshaping but not (so far) shrinking the addressable funnel, as increased physician engagement around obesity is driving more OSA screening and diagnosis
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate; medical device/insurance-reimbursed demand is relatively defensive versus discretionary consumer spending, though device replacement timing and DME provider capex can show some sensitivity to credit conditions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct impact (modest net debt); indirect effects through DME/HME provider financing costs and M&A funding costs
key_input_costs: Labor across manufacturing sites in Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, US, China, France

recent_developments.event: RBC Capital upgraded RMD to Outperform from Sector Perform (Sep 10, 2026); Citi raised price target to $240 from $235 (Sep 9, 2026); CEO Michael Farrell continued a pre-established Rule 10b5-1 selling program (~$1.1M sold Sep 8, 2026)

Reported Q4 FY2026 results: revenue $1.46-1.5B (+9% reported, +8% constant currency), non-GAAP EPS $2.95 (+16% YoY), beating consensus; issued first formal FY2027 guidance of 5-7% core revenue growth and non-GAAP EPS of $12.00-$12.25, with management flagging underlying core growth of 6-8%+ once Astral and divestiture dilution are excluded

FDA issued an early alert (July 15, 2026) regarding a potential high-risk issue with certain Astral 100/150 ventilators (supercapacitor leak risk); ResMed initiated a phased voluntary global field safety correction, prioritizing highest-risk patients given limited replacement-part availability

Acquired Noctrix Health (FDA De Novo-cleared restless legs syndrome neurostimulation device), expanding into an adjacent clinical sleep-health area; simultaneously entered a definitive agreement to sell the MatrixCare business (including HealthCareFirst, Citus, home health/hospice software) for $490M in an all-cash deal expected to close Q1 FY2027, as part of a portfolio-optimization push to refocus on core sleep, breathing and connected home healthcare

Acquired VirtuOx, a software-enabled independent diagnostic testing facility (IDTF), to build an end-to-end diagnosis-to-therapy pathway; expanded NightOwl home sleep apnea test availability across the US

Full-year revenue grew to $5.65B (from $5.15B in FY2025), gross margin expanded ~170bps to 61.1%, operating margin expanded to 33.4%, EPS grew to $10.43 (GAAP); generated $1.6B of free cash flow and returned over $1.0B to shareholders via buybacks and dividends (+70% YoY)

items.notes: First time management issued formal full-year revenue guidance; includes ~130bps drag from Astral field safety corrective action and dilution from the pending MatrixCare divestiture and recent Noctrix acquisition. Underlying core growth described by CFO as 'north of 6% to north of 8%' excluding these items

Implies roughly 15-17% growth off the FY2026 non-GAAP base; includes an estimated ~$0.15/share drag from the Astral correction, ~$0.30/share dilution from the MatrixCare divestiture, and ~$0.20/share dilution from Noctrix; core/underlying EPS growth implied at roughly 12-14% excluding these one-offs

items.target: Continued expansion (no specific numeric range disclosed in search results)
items.notes: FY2026 non-GAAP gross margin reached 62.3% in Q4 (+90bps YoY); management has consistently guided to ongoing margin expansion from mix and manufacturing efficiency
FY2026 capital returns of $1.0B+ were up more than 70% YoY; MatrixCare sale proceeds ($490M) expected to further support buyback capacity once the deal closes in Q1 FY2027

guidance.management_commentary: CFO Aaron Bloomer emphasized that headline FY2027 revenue and EPS guidance mask stronger underlying performance once the Astral field safety correction and portfolio changes (MatrixCare divestiture, Noctrix acquisition) are excluded, characterizing core growth as 'north of 6% to north of 8%.' Management framed FY2026 as a year of both strong core execution (record Q4 revenue, margin expansion, accelerating EPS growth) and active portfolio optimization (VirtuOx and Noctrix acquisitions to broaden the diagnosis-to-therapy funnel and clinical adjacencies, alongside the MatrixCare divestiture to refocus on core sleep/breathing/connected-home strategy).

bull_case: Dominant, durable market leadership in a large, underdiagnosed global sleep apnea market (fewer than 20% of US patients and under 10% elsewhere are diagnosed/treated), with a razor/blade replacement-parts annuity that supports high, expanding margins (61%+ gross margin, mid-30s% operating margin)

GLP-1 drugs have so far proven a net tailwind rather than a threat: ResMed's own real-world data on 2.5M+ patients shows GLP-1 use correlates with higher CPAP initiation and resupply rates, as increased physician engagement around obesity drives more OSA screening
Philips Respironics remains constrained by its US consent decree, leaving ResMed with an outsized share gain that could persist for years even as Philips eventually attempts to re-enter fully

Strong, accelerating financial performance and shareholder returns: FY2026 revenue +9-10%, EPS +16% (non-GAAP Q4), $1.6B free cash flow, and $1.0B+ of buybacks/dividends (+70% YoY), with FY2027 guidance implying continued double-digit underlying EPS growth

Disciplined portfolio management (VirtuOx and Noctrix acquisitions to expand the diagnosis-to-therapy funnel and clinical adjacencies; MatrixCare divestiture for $490M to refocus capital on the core, higher-return sleep/breathing business) signals capital discipline and strategic clarity
bear_case: Long-term GLP-1/anti-obesity drug adoption remains an unresolved structural risk: if sustained, significant weight loss materially reduces OSA prevalence/severity over a multi-year horizon, the total addressable market for CPAP could shrink even if near-term effects are positive; several analysts have kept RMD 'on watch' pending more data

Astral ventilator field safety correction (FDA early alert, phased fix due to parts shortages) creates near-term financial drag (~130bps revenue, ~$0.15 EPS in FY2027), litigation/reputational risk, and highlights execution risk in quality systems

Heavy dependence on US reimbursement policy exposes ResMed to unpredictable regulatory swings (DMEPOS competitive bidding changes, PFS conversion factor cuts, ACA/Medicaid funding reductions under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) that could pressure pricing and provider economics

Elevated valuation (consensus price target implies ~14% upside with a wide analyst range of $265-$345) leaves less room for error if GLP-1 headwinds intensify or Philips stages a stronger-than-expected US comeback

Residential Care Software segment has underdelivered on its cross-sell/synergy thesis, culminating in the MatrixCare divestiture — a tacit admission that not all diversification bets paid off, and simultaneous M&A/divestiture execution (VirtuOx, Noctrix, MatrixCare) adds integration complexity
